abstract:
The use of electric vehicles (EVs) is on the rise, and government initiatives are actively promoting their
adoption. However, compared to internal combustion vehicles (ICVs), EVs still have a limited range and
require more frequent recharging, making the availability of charging infrastructure a crucial factor in
their attractiveness. With the European Union’s plan to phase out the registration of new ICVs, it is
essential to evaluate the necessary infrastructure and its optimal location to meet the charging needs of
the population. Our objective is to develop functionality in MATSim that enables the simulation of charging behavior
by agents, allowing us to better understand the dynamics of EV charging and optimize the development
of the necessary infrastructure.
title: Simulating individual charging behaviour in MATSim

abstract:
On-demand mobility systems have been studied extensively for passenger transport. Agent-based simulation frameworks like MATSim allow to perform detailed quantitative analyses and answer a wide range of questions regarding these systems in a localized fashion. In the MATSim example, functionalities related to the on-demand systems are provided by the DVRP and DRT modules. The main target use case being systems serving passengers only, the functionality was implemented with the assumption that each request is associated to a passenger that takes one seat in a vehicle and that a vehicle's capacity can only be represented by the number of seats. In this work, technical developments were performed on the DRT and DVRP modules to remove those assumptions and allow the simulation of more complex systems. For instance, modelling services where vehicles have both a luggage capacity and a passenger capacity and where each traveller can have one or multiple luggages is now possible.
